interest: This docket sheet illustrates the State Department's systematic monitoring of Japanese military infrastructure expansion in North China during the uneasy period between the 1933 Tanggu Truce and the outbreak of the Second Sino-Japanese War in 1937. It highlights U.S. diplomatic reliance on local Chinese press sources, specifically the Tianjin Catholic daily I Shih Pao (Social Welfare), to track rumors and reports of Japanese aerodrome construction at Nankai. Additionally, the cross-reference to decimal file 793.94 (Sino-Japanese Relations) demonstrates how local intelligence on military base and barracks construction was integrated into broader diplomatic surveillance of Japanese encroachments in Hebei.
overview: This file (894.24593) consists of a single Department of State 'List of Papers' (Form DS-46) dated October 12, 1945, cataloguing documents concerning Japanese military bases in China between 1933 and 1936. The docket lists two October 1933 despatches from Frank P. Lockhart, American Consul General in Tianjin, regarding rumored Japanese plans to construct an aerodrome at Nankai and monitoring commentary from the local Chinese newspaper I Shih Pao. It also indexes an April 1936 despatch from Nelson T. Johnson, American Ambassador to China, reporting on the construction of Japanese military barracks and an aviation field at Tianjin, cross-referenced to decimal file 793.94/7904.

subfiles.summary: A Department of State List of Papers (Form DS-46) indexing records filed under decimal classification 894.24593 regarding Japanese military bases in China. It summarizes two 1933 despatches from Frank P. Lockhart in Tianjin to the Legation concerning Japanese plans for an airfield at Nankai, citing press despatches and the Chinese newspaper I Shih Pao. It additionally notes a 1936 communication from Nelson T. Johnson on the construction of Japanese barracks and an aviation field in Tianjin, referencing decimal file 793.94/7904.
